book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.d: Combat and data pack guide for Kingdom Come Combat
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.t: A guide to combat, combos, and data packs
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Directional attacks, defense, combos, and configuration
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.b: An introduction to lock-on and directional combat
Use the lock-on key to select a target. Move the mouse to change attack direction. Attacking, blocking, and dodging consume stamina. Attack direction affects your next stance and available combos.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Combos trigger when your recent attack directions match a learned sequence. The sequence is checked from the newest hits, so choose each direction before attacking and keep pressure without breaking the chain. Data packs may restrict a combo with required_weapon_tag; common values include swords, short_swords, longswords, axes, pickaxes, fighting_maces, maces, and heavy_weapons. heavy_weapons includes fighting maces, axes, and pickaxes.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.e: Stun weakened enemies and finish them with execution moves

A badly weakened enemy can be stunned by a hit that connects and is not perfectly blocked. The target must be below half health and low on stamina. During the short stun window, the execution icon appears near the lock-on crosshair. Hold attack while the icon is shown to start an execution. Executions pull the attacker into the move, keep the animation playing, and finish the victim at the end.

Executions use two branches: right or up stance selects one execution, while left or down stance selects the other. A successful execution restores all stamina and grants four levels of Analgesia and one level of Vitality, each for 25 seconds. Data packs configure execution moves in kingdom_come_combat/executions, allowed special targets in execution_targets, and select execution sets globally or per weapon.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.d: Combat data is loaded from data/<namespace>/kingdom_come_combat/. Data packs can extend or override combos, moves, weapons, armor, mobs, ai, passive_skills, and skill_books. Configuration is read again when data packs reload.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.a: How to obtain the manual, skills, and skill books

With Modonomicon installed, craft a book and an iron sword together (shapeless) to get the Kingdom Come Combat Manual; hold it and right-click to read it. Each skill book unlocks one combo or one book-only passive. Find them in ruins, temples, stronghold libraries, woodland mansions, ancient cities, and trial rewards, or buy them from level 2, 4, and 5 librarians. Open a skill book and turn to page two to learn it. Press K (rebindable) to review learned combos, passives, and skills you can buy with experience.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.s: The shared resource for offense, defense, and movement

Players have 100 base maximum stamina. Attacks use their move cost, dodges cost 18, forward steps cost 7, and normal blocks cost stamina based on incoming impact and block mitigation. By default, regeneration starts about two seconds after you spend stamina, at 1.2 per tick. Low health lowers maximum stamina, to no less than 60%; armor, injuries, weapons, shields, and skills can modify costs or recovery. Exhaustion weakens armor panels and can break guards, so avoid empty swings.

Blocking only works against frontal attacks. Pressing block starts with a perfect-block window followed by an imperfect-block window; block cannot be restarted during either window. Defaults are 0.4 seconds perfect and 0.5 seconds imperfect, both configurable. Non-classic mode requires the correct direction. In classic mode, holding block extends the imperfect phase after the perfect window. Player attacks always use the non-classic directional rule. Normal blocks spend stamina based on incoming impact and fail if stamina is insufficient.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.i: Localized wounds, bleeding, bandages, and recovery

Hits can injure arms, hands, torso, legs, or head; bleeding deals periodic damage. Injuries can weaken your attacks, health, movement, jumping, and other abilities. Equip bandages in matching armor slots: head for head wounds, chest for torso, arm, and hand wounds, and legs for leg wounds. Bandages stop bleeding first, then reduce wounds one level at a time down to one remaining level, losing durability as they work. Level 1-3 wounds recover about one level every ten minutes on their own; normal health regeneration speeds this up, and sleeping can spend food to treat minor wounds.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.t: Perfect defense, master strikes, and practical tactics

Read the incoming direction, then block shortly before impact with the matching direction. The default perfect window is 8 ticks (0.4 seconds), followed by a 10-tick (0.5 second) imperfect window; shields may extend the perfect window. A perfect block drains and interrupts the attacker and opens a counter window. A master strike requires attacking in the same direction during the enemy's brief startup. Preserve stamina, avoid misses, and dodge unblockable attacks.

The medium shield is a small shield with 130 durability and about 60% of a normal shield's defensive angle. It supports active vanilla-style blocking and can automatically imperfect-block combat attacks unless they come from the opposite guard direction, including shield-required attacks. Its perfect-block window is 40% longer and a successful perfect block disables the attacker for additional time. It never passively blocks arrows while locked on; projectiles require an active block window.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.p: Thrust, strike, slash, and posture pressure

Damage is split into thrust, strike, and slash. Thrust represents points and narrow penetration, slash represents cutting edges, and strike represents blunt force. Weapons, projectiles, moves, enchantments, durability, and hit location combine into those three incoming values. Armor compares each value against its matching defense panel for the covered body part, so a helmet may stop slash while still letting some strike or thrust through. Impact is separate posture pressure that drains stamina and can interrupt actions; blocked strike damage can still become impact.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.a: Coverage, three defense panels, and durability

Armor protects only configured body parts. On hit, thrust, strike, and slash penetration are compared separately against the matching defense of armor covering that location, then scaled by part protection. Multiple layers retain the best reduction for each type. Impact mitigation separately reduces stamina pressure up to 95%. Wear, low stamina, and armor-breach effects weaken defense; attacks damage the most effective protective layer. Aim for gaps or choose a damage type suited to the target.

The new armor system uses data-driven coverage, three defense panels, part protection, burden, impact mitigation, durability wear, and low-stamina weakening instead of relying only on vanilla armor value. Enchantments can feed those panels too: Heavy adds strike damage, Pointed adds thrust damage, and Sharpness still contributes weapon damage. Cushioning improves armor impact mitigation. Bracers copies an armor piece's shoulder protection panel to its arm coverage, replacing any existing arm panel. Stable, Powerful, and Rapid Fire modify ranged weapon handling.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.p: Apply potion effects to weapons and arrows

Hold a usable potion in the offhand and a valid weapon or at least four arrows in the main hand, then use the main hand. The coating action uses a bow-like third-person pose and takes about three seconds. Coating arrows consumes four arrows and the potion, then returns tipped arrows. Coating a weapon stores the potion on the weapon for a limited number of damaging hits; strong enough hits transfer a shortened version of the potion effects to the target. The empty bottle returns to your inventory as usual.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.g: Kingdom Come Combat adds five world game rules. /gamerule kccClassicMode true enables classic mode for non-player attacks. /gamerule kccPlayerDirectionalBlocking true makes player attacks require the correct block direction; false allows direction-free blocking against player attacks. /gamerule kccCombatSpeed <value> multiplies player and mob combat animation speed.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.w: Read directional guards, special attacks, and counter prompts

The yellow directional shield means a perfect block requires the correct guard direction. The plain shield means direction is ignored; this exception is reserved for vanilla-AI creature lunge and jump attacks. The red cannot-block icon means the attack must be dodged or avoided.

The perfect-block icon confirms a successful perfect block. The attack icon indicates that a perfect-counter window is open, so attack immediately. Direction branches on the lock-on crosshair show the current stance; move it to the guard direction required by the incoming attack.

In non-classic mode, ordinary attacks use the yellow directional shield and require a correct direction. Vanilla-AI creature lunges and jumps use the plain shield. Classic mode relaxes non-player attacks. Player attacks require direction only while kccPlayerDirectionalBlocking is enabled.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.g: /gamerule kccTrauma controls player injury, bleeding, and treatment consequences; mobs still use their combat behavior even when player trauma is disabled. /gamerule kccHardcoreMode hides lock-on crosshair aids and can be enabled with the KCC Super Hardcore option when creating a world. It is independent of vanilla Hardcore mode. These rules are saved per world, so data packs can tune combat while server owners keep final control.
createWorld.kingdom_come_combat.super_ha: Enables KCC's hardcore combat rule for this world. This is independent of vanilla Hardcore mode.
screen.kingdom_come_combat.hardships.des: Choose at least six hardships to accompany you. They are the burdens you must bear as you press onward.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.h: Momentum, stamina, braking, and sprint taps

Horses now use momentum and their own stamina. Tap sprint to build speed; holding movement keeps the horse moving forward while left and right steer the horse instead of instantly strafing. Turning is slower at high speed, and turning while moving reduces speed. Running above the threshold drains horse stamina, while walking or resting restores it. Jumping and hard braking cost stamina. If stamina reaches zero, the horse stops and needs a short recovery; pushing the horse too hard can panic it and throw the rider.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.c: Combo finishers are more than alternate animations. They can redirect the hit to a specific part such as face, crown, abdomen, or knee; adjust thrust, strike, and slash multipliers; add armor-breaking pressure; interrupt the target; or apply a short movement lock. Some combos are broad finishing cuts for groups, some punish exposed heads, and some target joints or armor gaps. A combo only triggers after it is learned; use the K skills screen to see the current data-pack values and inputs.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.l: Longsword use, material tiers, and recipes

Longswords have extended reach and unlock dedicated two-handed techniques. Wood, stone, copper, gold, iron, diamond, and netherite variants share one recipe: place the material in the top-center slot, fill the middle row with three of the same material, and place a stick in the bottom-center slot. Material tier changes base attack and durability; thrust, strike, slash, and weapon condition still shape final performance.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.f: Heavy mace use, material tiers, and recipes

Fighting maces are heavy weapons built around strike damage, armor breaking, and impact. They can use heavy weapon combos and are suited to armored targets that resist clean cuts. Copper, gold, iron, diamond, and netherite variants share one recipe: leave the top-left empty, place material in the top-center and top-right, place a stick in the center and material in the middle-right, then place a stick in the bottom-left. There are no wooden or stone fighting maces.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.p: Combat with tridents, spears, and poleaxes

Tridents, spears, and poleaxes are polearms. They require both hands, cannot be used while the offhand is occupied, and have no upper stance. Polearms can perfect-block attacks from any direction and do not automatically change stance afterward. An unlocked attack defaults to the lower thrust when the attack button is released. Poleaxes use material, stick, material across the top row with sticks in the center slots below; the netherite poleaxe is upgraded from the diamond variant in a smithing table.
book.kingdom_come_combat.combat_manual.f: The hand cannon is a high-power ranged weapon. Hold firearm cartridges in the offhand and use the cannon in the main hand to load it; use it again after loading to fire. Loading leaves you vulnerable. Craft the cannon from five iron ingots and a stick. Craft one iron nugget and one gunpowder (shapeless) into four cartridges. Projectiles use their own thrust, strike, and slash panels against armor covering the hit part. Headshots are resolved through the same localized system, so a shot can strike protected crown or side-head areas, while an exposed face is far more dangerous.

Allows special right-click abilities from third-party weapons only while not locked on. While locked on, right click continues to use KCC blocking.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.combat: Players and targets use this distance; active mod AI mobs keep this value minus 0.2 meters from each other.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.collis: Maximum client radius for loading animated model and weapon collision boxes. Defaults to 8 meters; boxes load on demand, or continuously while F3+B is enabled.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.vanill: Item IDs listed here use Minecraft's vanilla entity attack and are not intercepted by custom combat.
Search by item name or registry ID; saving adds it to the list above.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.reach_: Scale hitboxes from entity reach, attack range, and compatible entity-attack range modifiers supplied by the main-hand weapon itself.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.blocki: When enabled, holding block slows player movement; disabling it removes the additional blocking slowdown.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.mounte: When enabled, attacks made while riding a horse or camel use the KCC combat system instead of vanilla attacks.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.reach_: Hitbox Scale per Block of Reach
Percentage that hitbox length changes for each block of entity attack range added or removed by the weapon; defaults to 20%.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.vanill: Entity registry IDs listed here are attacked through Minecraft's vanilla attack flow.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.mob_to: When disabled, player attacks interrupt mob attacks whenever final mitigated impact exceeds the mob AI toughness value.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.always: When enabled, any unblocked player attack interrupts mob attacks and ignores mob toughness, even if armor is not penetrated.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.legacy: Controlled by the server for every player. Uses animation-formula estimates when enabled; otherwise rendered bone hitboxes take priority.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.lightw: Major server-wide switch. Removes bleeding and injuries, custom armor, weapon panels, localized damage, and toughness. Melee damage becomes vanilla weapon damage times the highest of the move's three panel modifiers; only head hits deal 1.5x damage. Vanilla damage, armor reduction, hit handling, and projectile mechanics are restored, weapon attribute tooltips are hidden, and every hit may interrupt attacks.
Reduces enemy block and perfect-block chances by (100% - current chance) and makes enemies attack slightly less often.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.client: Controlled by the server. When enabled, clients may report arrows that miss vanilla boxes but intersect mod hurtboxes; the server still verifies every report.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.experi: Makes illagers and undead mobs hostile to each other. Disabled by default.
config.kingdom_come_combat.server.permis: Only players with permission to use cheats can change server-wide settings.
config.kingdom_come_combat.error.invalid: Invalid item ID. Use a full ID such as minecraft:spyglass.
